Estimate a sparse Gaussian graphical model on a filtered graph (LoGo)

Source: R/logo.R
logo_network.Rd

logo_network() estimates a sparse Gaussian graphical model on a filtered graph with the Local-Global (LoGo) method. LoGo works in two steps: it first chooses the network structure by information filtering with the triangulated maximally filtered graph (TMFG), and then estimates the partial correlations as the maximum-likelihood Gaussian graphical model on that graph (Barfuss et al., 2016).

The TMFG retains the strongest correlations under the constraint that the graph stays planar and is built from tetrahedra (four-variable cliques), which fixes the number of edges at \(3(p - 2)\) for \(p\) variables. Because the graph is decomposable, the maximum-likelihood estimate has a closed form, assembled from the inverses of small local correlation matrices, so no penalty or iterative fitting is needed. The model is estimated from raw data or from a correlation matrix with its sample size.

logo_network() returns the partial-correlation network of this model, the maximum-likelihood network on the TMFG graph, which certificate() checks.

The graph alone, with correlations as edge weights, is returned by tmfg_network(). For a network whose sparsity is chosen by the data use ebic_glasso() or ggm_modselect(). The model is the one fitted by NetworkToolbox::LoGo().

Usage

logo_network(
  data = NULL,
  cor_matrix = NULL,
  n = NULL,
  cor_method = c("pearson", "spearman", "kendall", "auto"),
  threshold = 0,
  na_method = c("pairwise", "listwise"),
  labels = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A numeric data frame or matrix with one row per observation. Not needed when cor_matrix is given.

cor_matrix

A correlation matrix to use instead of data; a covariance matrix is rescaled to a correlation matrix. n is then required.

n

Sample size, required with cor_matrix and recorded on the result: a single finite number >= 1. Ignored when data is given.

cor_method

Correlation computed from data: "pearson" (default), "spearman", "kendall", or "auto" (polychoric and polyserial correlations for ordinal items; see cor_auto()).

threshold

Absolute partial correlation below which an edge is set to zero after estimation: a single number >= 0. Default 0. A logical value is refused. A positive value leaves the certificate missing.

na_method

Handling of missing values in data: "pairwise" (default) or "listwise". See ebic_glasso().

labels

Optional node labels, one unique label per node of the network.

Value

A fitted network of class psychnet (psychnet) whose edge weights are partial correlations. as.data.frame() returns one row per edge with columns from, to and weight; certificate() reports the check. The object also stores the precision matrix (precision), the TMFG graph as a logical matrix (support) and the correlation matrix (cor_matrix).

Details

With \(C\) the four-variable cliques and \(T\) the three-variable separators of the TMFG, the precision matrix is $$\Theta = \sum_{c \in C} [S_{cc}^{-1}]^0 - \sum_{t \in T} [S_{tt}^{-1}]^0,$$ where \([\cdot]^0\) pads a block with zeros to the full size. The certificate is computed by ggm_support_kkt() with the TMFG as the graph. After a positive threshold it is missing; print() still shows the value for the network before thresholding.

The closed form needs every clique and separator block to be invertible. A block that is singular or nearly so (reciprocal condition number below 1e-10, as with duplicate or collinear variables) is refused rather than approximated, as is a precision matrix whose certificate exceeds 1e-6.

Conditions

psychnet_singular (error, also of class psychnet_bad_input) when a clique or separator block is singular or nearly so, or the precision matrix fails its certificate; psychnet_bad_input when there are fewer than four variables, an argument is out of range, threshold is logical, cor_matrix is not a finite, symmetric, positive semi-definite matrix with a positive diagonal, n is missing with cor_matrix, or labels do not match the nodes; psychnet_constant_variable (warning) when a constant or all-missing column is dropped.

References

Barfuss, W., Massara, G. P., Di Matteo, T., & Aste, T. (2016). Parsimonious modeling with information filtering networks. Physical Review E, 94(6), 062306. doi:10.1103/PhysRevE.94.062306

Massara, G. P., Di Matteo, T., & Aste, T. (2016). Network filtering for big data: Triangulated maximally filtered graph. Journal of Complex Networks, 5(2), 161-178. doi:10.1093/comnet/cnw015

See also

tmfg_network() for the filtered graph; certificate() and ggm_support_kkt() for the check; psychnet(), which routes method = "logo" here; psychnet for the result.

Examples

set.seed(1)
x <- matrix(stats::rnorm(300 * 6), 300, 6)
logo_network(x)
#> <psychnet> logo network
#>   nodes: 6   edges: 12   (undirected)
#>   optimality (KKT residual): 4.44e-16
